In 2006, Star Health and Allied Insurance became India's first standalone Health Insurance company. Twenty years later, the launch of Value Plus marks the next chapter, and India's leading publications carried the story.

The Economic Times, covered Star Health's two-decade milestone alongside the launch of Value Plus.

Value Plus is an affordable Health Insurance offering designed to bring wider health protection to young Indians in Tier 2, 3 and 4 cities at nearly 20% lower premiums. It offers high sum-insured covers from ₹7.5 lakh to ₹25 lakh through a curated network of 11,000+ quality hospitals.

20 years in. The next chapter begins now.

"Insurance growth in India is no longer a metro story. The next wave will come from Tier II, Tier III and Tier IV markets.”

In an interview with Shine Jacob from Business Standard, our MD and CEO Anand Roy laid out why retail health penetration in smaller towns is non-negotiable for the country's Insurance for All by 2047 vision.

The first 20 years helped build India's health insurance category. The next 20 will be about taking protection deeper into Bharat.

"GWP up to ₹5,968 crore. Net profit up to ₹111 cr."

That was the headline takeaway in The Economic Times, on Star Health and Allied Insurance's Q4 FY26 results.

The coverage walked through the company's Q4 numbers. Net profit at ₹111 crore, a multi-fold jump from ₹50 lakh in the same quarter last year. Net Premium at ₹5,599 crore, up from ₹4,820 crore YoY. Total income at ₹4,545 crore, up from ₹3,989 crore YoY. And the underwriting loss narrowed sharply to ₹154 crore from ₹275 crore in the year-ago period.

Star Health has launched 32 Arogya Seva Kendras (ASK) under its CSR initiative to strengthen access to community-level primary healthcare across nine states, with the goal of impacting over one million lives.

In partnership with Piramal Swasthya (part of Piramal Foundation), these clinics will provide free primary healthcare services, including:

* MBBS doctor consultations
* Screening for hypertension, diabetes, and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs)
* Laboratory diagnostics and essential medicines
* Health counselling and awareness sessions
* Adult pneumococcal vaccination support, with expertise from Pfizer

With hypertension prevalence ranging from 20–40% and diabetes affecting up to 29% of adults in certain districts, this initiative highlights the urgent need for preventive and accessible primary care to address India’s growing NCD burden.

A meaningful step toward healthcare equity ensuring quality primary care reaches communities early, consistently, and close to home.

Star Health reported strong Q3 FY26 performance, supported by premium growth, disciplined underwriting, and improved operating efficiency.
The quarter reflects sustained focus on profitability, claims excellence, and customer trust.

I had a very disappointing claim experience with TATA AIG and Policybazaar.
My car (two scratches on the same left side) was given to Maruti Vasai East on 22 Nov. The service center assured it was a minor claim, but TATA AIG approved only the smallest scratch for ~₹4,000 against an 18k estimate.

No one answered calls, emails only gave automated replies, and after asking Policybazaar for help, even their “24-hour promise” resulted in no action except a WhatsApp group and formal calls. Eventually, the service center asked me to take the car back because no progress was happening.

I was even planning to renew a 2-year zero-dep plan (after repeated calls from both teams), but this experience has made me lose trust. When it comes to selling a policy, they call 10 times a day — but during claim time, there is no support.

Posting this so others are aware before purchasing.
